input.rationale: Receipt 974fc0c0b07644169bfb205e8a4e92c7 (exit 0) is the corrected successor and all five comparisons are complete and hold: the transfer aimed at the demoted non-voter returned nil within 1ms while the sitting leader was already Follower and the named destination was only Candidate (indices 1 and 2 of the comparison set, both on event index 1); the destination never led during the eight second watch and the cluster was observed without a leader at some 20ms sample (event index 2); and the control aimed at a voter returned nil within 3ms with that voter leading and no leaderless sample (event indices 4 and 5). The earlier receipt's violated comparison is superseded by this one rather than reinterpreted: it asserted a field whose meaning was 'the old leader was seen leading at some point in the watch', which the recovery satisfied, whereas the successor asserts the interruption directly and the destination and control predicates are unchanged. The account for this question is therefore no longer conditional on my declaration; the recovery remains a limit on how far the consequence reaches, not on the mechanism.

limitations: One treatment execution and one control, in-memory transports in one process, uniform timings; how long a leaderless interval could last in a cluster with slower timings or fewer reachable voters is not bounded by this receipt.

The caller's observation is the future's error value only; the harness does not distinguish a handover from a fresh election through any other client-visible signal, and it does not read the transfer branch's internal path, so the success is attributed to the lost-leadership branch from the timing pattern (leader already Follower, destination still Candidate) rather than from inside that branch.
The destination is a node demoted through DemoteVoter; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage reach the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not exercised.

knowledge.statement: In a 4-node cluster whose configuration is voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter, LeadershipTransferToServer aimed at the non-voter returns success (nil) within about a millisecond while the sitting leader is already Follower and the named destination is only Candidate; the destination never leads during the following eight seconds and the cluster is observed without a leader at some 20ms sample before a different node wins the fresh election. With the identical call aimed at a voter, success is returned in about three milliseconds, the named destination leads, and no leaderless sample occurs.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-memory transports, fully connected, uniform HeartbeatTimeout 2s and LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s, CommitTimeout 200ms; the non-voter is produced by DemoteVoter before the transfer; one execution of each case.

interpretations.rationale: What the corrected comparisons establish: (1) the transfer future reports success although the named destination holds no vote; (2) at the moment that success arrives the sitting leader is no longer Leader; (3) the named destination never leads during the watch; (4) the cluster is observed without a leader during the watch, so the existing leadership was interrupted rather than handed over; (5) the control with a voter destination reports success and that destination leads. Source-wise each step has an owner: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not filter the destination (raft.go:2184-2207) while pickServer does (raft.go:2163-2182); TimeoutNow turns the destination into a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote regardless of suffrage (raft.go:2209-2214); voters that receive its RequestVote adopt the higher term and step down before the suffrage check rejects the vote (raft.go:1660-1690), which is what removes the sitting leader; and the transfer branch reports success on the lost-leadership path without checking whether the requested destination became leader (raft.go:733-737). The defect claim is therefore: naming a destination the configuration does not allow to lead yields a success result indistinguishable from a real handover, while the sitting leadership is interrupted and a fresh election - which the caller did not ask for and which need not restore the same node - decides the outcome. The recovery is real and bounds the consequence (the cluster elected a new leader within the same eight second window), so nothing is claimed about sustained unavailability.
counterevidence: The interruption is bounded: in both receipts the cluster elected a leader again inside the watch window, and no leaderless interval longer than the watch is claimed, so any phrasing that the cluster is left unavailable is contradicted.

The earlier receipt's watch sampled every 100ms and recorded the old leader leading again inside the window; that observation remains true of that run but is not part of this account's predicates, which assert the destination and interruption instead.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control per receipt; uniform timings and fully connected in-memory transports in one process.

investigations.question: When a leader keeps only a non-voter reachable, does VerifyLeader (the client-visible 'still leader' confirmation) return success even though no quorum of voters replied?
investigations.hypothesis: verifyLeader seeds votes=1 (self) and quorumSize=voters/2+1, then registers the verifyFuture on every followerReplication object, including the ones created for non-voters. A non-voter's successful AppendEntries response reaches notifyAll(true) and increments votes without any suffrage check, so with voters {L,B,D} and non-voter C, L can reach votes==quorumSize==2 with only C's acknowledgement.
investigations.discriminator: Hold topology, partition and timing fixed in a real 4-node in-memory cluster and change exactly one property at a time: (a) demote the node kept with the leader from voter to non-voter through DemoteVoter, (b) keep it a voter, (c) keep it a non-voter but cut the leader from everyone. The prediction is success in (a) and non-success in (b) and (c); the same outcome in (b) or (c) would refute the suffrage-attribution explanation.

gaps.question: Does the false confirmation extend past the leader's own lease window, i.e. does VerifyLeader report success while a different node already holds leadership and has committed a write that the partitioned leader's FSM lacks? The window is bounded because ValidateConfig requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout and checkLeaderLease counts only voters, so the partitioned leader steps down within about one lease interval; a successor harness with per-node timing (long leader lease, short follower election timers) is needed to place a voter-majority election inside that window.

investigations.question: After a committed voter-to-non-voter transition, can a peer's own configuration view keep reporting the old suffrage for seconds while the other peers already report the change, and if so what makes that peer lag on the configuration entry?
investigations.hypothesis: A configuration entry updates a peer's latest configuration only when it is newly appended (appendEntries processes configuration entries of newEntries) or installed through a snapshot; a peer that has not appended the entry keeps reporting its previous configuration. If the leader's replication to one peer stalls - for example a stalled append pipeline that never re-enters RPC mode - that peer would keep the old view while the others commit and apply the change.
investigations.discriminator: Sample every node's own configuration view and LastIndex continuously (for example every 20ms) across the DemoteVoter call and for at least ten seconds afterwards, in the per-node timing used by the extended-window scenario, and repeat the run several times. A peer whose view stays old while its LastIndex also stops advancing would show a replication stall; a peer whose LastIndex has already passed the configuration index while its view stays old would instead point at the configuration-entry processing path; view and index converging within milliseconds in every run would leave the earlier single observation as an unexplained artefact.
counterevidence: Every applicable observation in 0adb78b8f8da429f865c2abb097b4ff8 answers this question negatively for the tested construction: all twelve node observations converged in 0-20ms, and no node had a stale view after its own LastIndex reached the configuration index (indices 4-7, 12-15, 20-23).
The earlier receipt 24679b2ecdd54556adf91882ce0f8b0c carries the same measurements (indices 1-4) with comparisons that were incomplete only because of my admission declaration.
limitations: The refutation is scoped to a healthy, fully connected, unloaded in-memory cluster with this per-node timing; neither contending client traffic nor a deliberately stalled append pipeline was exercised, and the entry-delivery path (appendEntries deciding on newEntries, snapshot install) was traced by reading rather than perturbed.

The sighting that opened the question - near_node_self_voter true after a three second settle loop in receipt 2444815cf0d84e06917efa1091d12257 index 0 - was not reproduced, and its cause is still unidentified; the differences I could name (waiting for followers before the transition, and the per-node timing) were both exercised natively without reproducing it.

investigations.question: When LeadershipTransferToServer names a server that holds no vote, what does the caller observe, what happens to the existing leadership, and does the requested destination ever take leadership?
investigations.hypothesis: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not inspect the target's suffrage, so a non-voter target is contacted with TimeoutNow; timeoutNow makes it a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote, so it campaigns in the next term. Every voter that receives that RequestVote adopts the higher term and steps down before the suffrage check rejects the vote, so the current leader loses leadership although the target can never win; the transfer future then reports success through the leftLeaderLoop branch, which responds nil without checking whether the requested destination became leader.
investigations.discriminator: Compare the identical call aimed at a non-voter and at a voter in the same 4-node cluster: if the leader merely loses leadership while the requested destination never leads, the suffrage-blind transfer path is established; if the non-voter target leads, or if leadership is unaffected, the explanation is refuted. The control must show that the same call with a voter target results in that target leading.

knowledge.statement: On a leader, verifyLeader() registers the pending verifyFuture on every entry of leaderState.replState and compares accumulated votes against a quorum size computed only from voters; every followerReplication whose AppendEntries/heartbeat response reports success calls notifyAll(true), which increments verifyFuture.votes without consulting the peer's ServerSuffrage. Therefore a peer recorded as Nonvoter (or Staging) contributes a vote to the VerifyLeader confirmation.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the peer is present in r.configurations.latest.Servers with Suffrage != Voter and is reachable by the leader's transport; the verifyFuture is still pending (notifyCh != nil) when the response arrives.

knowledge.statement: In a real 4-node in-memory cluster whose latest configuration has voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter reachable by the leader, a VerifyLeader call issued immediately after the leader is cut off from far1 and far2 returns nil (success) with the leader still in Leader state, within the same millisecond as the partition, in three independent attempts on each of two receipts. Repeating the identical scenario with that reachable node still a voter, or with the non-voter also unreachable, returns "leadership lost while committing log" about one LeaderLeaseTimeout later instead.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; latest configuration voters=3, nonvoters=1 (quorum_size=voters/2+1=2); transport routes to the two far voters removed while routes to the non-voter stay intact; HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout (3s treatment, 2s controls), ProtocolVersion 3; in-memory transport and stores in one process.

knowledge.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil at 0ms after the partition, and answers nil again at 5509ms when one of the far nodes is already Leader, while that node commits a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L still Leader, applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" at 20003ms, when L's lease expires.

knowledge.statement: In a healthy 4-node cluster (leader HeartbeatTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s, the node to be demoted 6s, the two far voters 3s, only the leader bootstrapped) a committed DemoteVoter transition is reflected in every node's own GetConfiguration view of that peer's suffrage within 0-20ms of the leader's commit, measured every 20ms for ten seconds, in four runs; no node's view was still old at a sample where its own LastIndex had already reached the configuration entry's index.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons and their meaning, kept separate from the defect judgment. Comparison 0 (anomaly prediction: success with only the demoted non-voter reachable) holds on index 2. Comparison 1 (anomaly prediction for the extension, antecedent new_leader_exists true) holds on index 3: the same confirmation is answered with nil at 5509ms while a competing node holds leadership and while the answering leader is still Leader with a 20s lease. Comparison 2 (antecedent new_leader_fsm_has_write true, applicability old_leader_is_leader true) holds on index 4: the payload committed by the competing leader at index 5 is absent from the old leader's FSM, whose applied index is 3 — so a client that follows the documented pattern (confirm, then read) reads state that omits a committed write. Comparison 3 (control) holds on index 7: the identical construction and per-node timing without the demotion yields no competitor and no success, ending in leadership loss at 20003ms. Defect claim: the confirmation is computed against a voter-only quorum (raft.go:1086-1093) but credited by an unfiltered vote path (raft.go:965-987 registering every followerReplication; replication.go:100-111 notifying each; future.go:274-293 counting without suffrage), while the target's own definition states non-voters are not considered for elections or commitment (configuration.go:16-18); therefore a client can be told it is safe to treat a leader that has lost every other voter as leader for the whole configured lease interval, even after a different node holds leadership and has committed writes the old leader never received. The controls in the two earlier receipts (indices 12 and 15 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623, indices 11 and 14 of df528a8a25a04cbd9fb1cc12319f3467) already excluded reachability and kept the same reachable node as a voter, so the enabling property remains the unfiltered vote attribution.

answers.101498ecfbb945e0b48676dd9e9f4172-gap-0: Yes, and the bound is the leader's own lease rather than the election interval. In the extended-window execution the partitioned leader answered VerifyLeader successfully at 0ms and again at 5509ms (index 2 and 3), while the voter majority had already elected its own leader and committed a write at index 5 (index 4); the old leader remained Leader at applied index 3 with that write absent from its FSM. The lease path that eventually ends this state is checkLeaderLease, which counts only voters whose last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout (raft.go:1036-1060), so the window lasts as long as the configured lease; ValidateConfig only requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout (config.go:366-371), so the 20s used here is a legal configuration and the exposure is bounded by that configured value, not by the followers' 3s election time.

The source path accounts for each part: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not filter the destination (raft.go:2184-2207) while pickServer does (raft.go:2163-2182); TimeoutNow turns the destination into a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote regardless of suffrage (raft.go:2209-2214); a voter receiving that candidate's RequestVote adopts the higher term and steps down before the suffrage check rejects the vote (raft.go:1660-1690), which is why the sitting leader loses leadership; and the transfer branch reports success on the leftLeaderLoop path without checking whether the requested destination became leader (raft.go:733-737). The claim is therefore scoped and conditional: a caller that names a destination which the configuration does not allow to lead receives a success result it cannot distinguish from a real handover, and in exchange the cluster suffers a leadership interruption and a fresh election that the caller did not request. The consequence is bounded - the cluster recovered in the same window, in this run by re-electing the very node it had just lost - and that recovery is the counterevidence that limits the phrasing rather than the mechanism.
counterevidence: Comparison 2 is violated by a valid witness: the emitted field old_leader_still_leader records that the old leader was observed leading during the eight second watch, because after the disruption it won the fresh election (index 2, leader_after_id is the old leader's own id). Any phrasing that leadership is lost for good, or that the cluster is left without a leader, is contradicted by this observation.

The watch samples states every 100ms, so a leaderless interval shorter than that interval inside the window would not be recorded; the receipt shows the interruption through index 1 (old leader Follower, target Candidate, nil result) rather than through a measured leaderless duration.

The nil result has two possible provenance paths in the transfer branch (the leader left the leaderLoop, or the wait for the destination timed out); this receipt shows the immediate return with the old leader already Follower and the target still Candidate, which matches the leftLeaderLoop path, but the harness does not read that branch directly.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control in the same run, uniform timings (HeartbeatTimeout 2s, LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s), in-memory transports in one process, fully connected throughout.
The destination is a node demoted through DemoteVoter; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage reach the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not exercised.
The caller's observation is the future's error value only; the harness does not attempt to distinguish a handover from a fresh election through any other client-visible signal.
The eight second watch bounds nothing about how long a leaderless interval could last in a cluster with slower timings or fewer reachable voters.

result.summary: Recorded the corrected account for the leadership-transfer line from CheckRun 974fc0c0b07644169bfb205e8a4e92c7 (exit 0), where all five comparisons are complete and hold: the transfer aimed at the demoted non-voter returned nil within 1ms while the sitting leader was already Follower and the named destination only Candidate; the destination never led during the eight second watch and the cluster was observed without a leader at some 20ms sample before a different node won the fresh election; the control aimed at a voter returned nil within 3ms with that voter leading and no leaderless sample. The earlier receipt's mis-declared predicate is superseded rather than reinterpreted, and both receipts are cited with joint_history. Conclusion holds, defect claim asserted and scoped: naming a destination the configuration does not allow to lead yields a success result indistinguishable from a real handover while the sitting leadership is interrupted and a fresh election decides the outcome, with the bounded recovery kept as counterevidence against any sustained-unavailability phrasing. A durable fact was promoted for the transfer behaviour, the question is marked explained with its unresolved limits stated, and no further experiment was submitted.

investigations.question: When a leader keeps only a non-voter reachable, does VerifyLeader (the client-visible 'still leader' confirmation) return success even though no quorum of voters replied?
investigations.hypothesis: verifyLeader seeds votes=1 (self) and quorumSize=voters/2+1, then registers the verifyFuture on every followerReplication object, including the ones created for non-voters. A non-voter's successful AppendEntries response reaches notifyAll(true) and increments votes without any suffrage check, so with voters {L,B,D} and non-voter C, L can reach votes==quorumSize==2 with only C's acknowledgement.
investigations.discriminator: Hold topology, partition and timing fixed in a real 4-node in-memory cluster and change exactly one property at a time: (a) demote the node kept with the leader from voter to non-voter through DemoteVoter, (b) keep it a voter, (c) keep it a non-voter but cut the leader from everyone. The prediction is success in (a) and non-success in (b) and (c); the same outcome in (b) or (c) would refute the suffrage-attribution explanation.

gaps.question: Does the false confirmation extend past the leader's own lease window, i.e. does VerifyLeader report success while a different node already holds leadership and has committed a write that the partitioned leader's FSM lacks? The window is bounded because ValidateConfig requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout and checkLeaderLease counts only voters, so the partitioned leader steps down within about one lease interval; a successor harness with per-node timing (long leader lease, short follower election timers) is needed to place a voter-majority election inside that window.

investigations.question: After a committed voter-to-non-voter transition, can a peer's own configuration view keep reporting the old suffrage for seconds while the other peers already report the change, and if so what makes that peer lag on the configuration entry?
investigations.hypothesis: A configuration entry updates a peer's latest configuration only when it is newly appended (appendEntries processes configuration entries of newEntries) or installed through a snapshot; a peer that has not appended the entry keeps reporting its previous configuration. If the leader's replication to one peer stalls - for example a stalled append pipeline that never re-enters RPC mode - that peer would keep the old view while the others commit and apply the change.
investigations.discriminator: Sample every node's own configuration view and LastIndex continuously (for example every 20ms) across the DemoteVoter call and for at least ten seconds afterwards, in the per-node timing used by the extended-window scenario, and repeat the run several times. A peer whose view stays old while its LastIndex also stops advancing would show a replication stall; a peer whose LastIndex has already passed the configuration index while its view stays old would instead point at the configuration-entry processing path; view and index converging within milliseconds in every run would leave the earlier single observation as an unexplained artefact.
counterevidence: Every applicable observation in 0adb78b8f8da429f865c2abb097b4ff8 answers this question negatively for the tested construction: all twelve node observations converged in 0-20ms, and no node had a stale view after its own LastIndex reached the configuration index (indices 4-7, 12-15, 20-23).
The earlier receipt 24679b2ecdd54556adf91882ce0f8b0c carries the same measurements (indices 1-4) with comparisons that were incomplete only because of my admission declaration.
limitations: The refutation is scoped to a healthy, fully connected, unloaded in-memory cluster with this per-node timing; neither contending client traffic nor a deliberately stalled append pipeline was exercised, and the entry-delivery path (appendEntries deciding on newEntries, snapshot install) was traced by reading rather than perturbed.

The sighting that opened the question - near_node_self_voter true after a three second settle loop in receipt 2444815cf0d84e06917efa1091d12257 index 0 - was not reproduced, and its cause is still unidentified; the differences I could name (waiting for followers before the transition, and the per-node timing) were both exercised natively without reproducing it.

investigations.question: When LeadershipTransferToServer names a server that holds no vote, what does the caller observe, what happens to the existing leadership, and does the requested destination ever take leadership?
investigations.hypothesis: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not inspect the target's suffrage, so a non-voter target is contacted with TimeoutNow; timeoutNow makes it a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote, so it campaigns in the next term. Every voter that receives that RequestVote adopts the higher term and steps down before the suffrage check rejects the vote, so the current leader loses leadership although the target can never win; the transfer future then reports success through the leftLeaderLoop branch, which responds nil without checking whether the requested destination became leader.
investigations.discriminator: Compare the identical call aimed at a non-voter and at a voter in the same 4-node cluster: if the leader merely loses leadership while the requested destination never leads, the suffrage-blind transfer path is established; if the non-voter target leads, or if leadership is unaffected, the explanation is refuted. The control must show that the same call with a voter target results in that target leading.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control, in-memory transports in one process, uniform timings; how long a leaderless interval could last in a cluster with slower timings or fewer reachable voters is not bounded by this receipt.

The caller's observation is the future's error value only; the harness does not distinguish a handover from a fresh election through any other client-visible signal, and it does not read the transfer branch's internal path, so the success is attributed to the lost-leadership branch from the timing pattern (leader already Follower, destination still Candidate) rather than from inside that branch.

knowledge.statement: On a leader, verifyLeader() registers the pending verifyFuture on every entry of leaderState.replState and compares accumulated votes against a quorum size computed only from voters; every followerReplication whose AppendEntries/heartbeat response reports success calls notifyAll(true), which increments verifyFuture.votes without consulting the peer's ServerSuffrage. Therefore a peer recorded as Nonvoter (or Staging) contributes a vote to the VerifyLeader confirmation.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the peer is present in r.configurations.latest.Servers with Suffrage != Voter and is reachable by the leader's transport; the verifyFuture is still pending (notifyCh != nil) when the response arrives.

knowledge.statement: In a real 4-node in-memory cluster whose latest configuration has voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter reachable by the leader, a VerifyLeader call issued immediately after the leader is cut off from far1 and far2 returns nil (success) with the leader still in Leader state, within the same millisecond as the partition, in three independent attempts on each of two receipts. Repeating the identical scenario with that reachable node still a voter, or with the non-voter also unreachable, returns "leadership lost while committing log" about one LeaderLeaseTimeout later instead.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; latest configuration voters=3, nonvoters=1 (quorum_size=voters/2+1=2); transport routes to the two far voters removed while routes to the non-voter stay intact; HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout (3s treatment, 2s controls), ProtocolVersion 3; in-memory transport and stores in one process.

knowledge.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil at 0ms after the partition, and answers nil again at 5509ms when one of the far nodes is already Leader, while that node commits a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L still Leader, applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" at 20003ms, when L's lease expires.
knowledge.conditions: Real 4-node in-memory cluster, only L bootstrapped; near node demoted voter->non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API; transport routes between {L, C} and {far1, far2} removed in both directions; CommitTimeout 200ms; leader lease 20s; single execution.

knowledge.statement: In a healthy 4-node cluster (leader HeartbeatTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s, the node to be demoted 6s, the two far voters 3s, only the leader bootstrapped) a committed DemoteVoter transition is reflected in every node's own GetConfiguration view of that peer's suffrage within 0-20ms of the leader's commit, measured every 20ms for ten seconds, in four runs; no node's view was still old at a sample where its own LastIndex had already reached the configuration entry's index.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-memory transports, no partition, no load, no restart; the transition is a single DemoteVoter call on the leader with prevIndex 0; followers are otherwise caught up (LastIndex >= 2) before the change in the successor runs.

knowledge.statement: In a 4-node cluster whose configuration is voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter, LeadershipTransferToServer aimed at the non-voter returns success (nil) within about a millisecond while the sitting leader is already Follower and the named destination is only Candidate; the destination never leads during the following eight seconds and the cluster is observed without a leader at some 20ms sample before a different node wins the fresh election. With the identical call aimed at a voter, success is returned in about three milliseconds, the named destination leads, and no leaderless sample occurs.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-memory transports, fully connected, uniform HeartbeatTimeout 2s and LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s, CommitTimeout 200ms; the non-voter is produced by DemoteVoter before the transfer; one execution of each case.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons: comparison 0 predicted the anomaly (success while only a non-voter is reachable) and comparison 1 and 2 predicted that nothing else produces it; all three are complete and hold over every applicable observation (treatment indices 2, 6, 9; control indices 12 and 15), and the controls differ from the treatment in exactly one property each (suffrage of the reachable node; reachability of that same non-voter). The defect claim is separate from those predicate results: the leader's client-visible confirmation that it may still be treated as leader is satisfied by an acknowledgement from a peer that the target itself defines as not considered for elections or commitment (configuration.go:16-18), while the quorum it is compared against counts voters only (raft.go:1086-1093) and the vote attribution is unfiltered (future.go:274-293 via replication.go:100-111). Under the documented purpose of the call (api.go:880-882) a client that gates reads on VerifyLeader can therefore be told it is safe to read a leader that has lost every voter except itself, until its own lease expires; the first receipt's index 3 shows the majority side committing a write (index 5) that never reached that leader's FSM (applied index 3, write absent). The remaining uncertainty is the length of that window, recorded as the open gap.

counterevidence: Index 3 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623: in the only attempt where the voter majority elected a new leader and committed 'assurance-stale-write' (index 5, present in the new leader's FSM, absent from the partitioned leader's, which was at applied index 3), the partitioned leader had already become Follower at the 3386ms sample, so this receipt does not witness a successful confirmation issued after the majority had a competing leader.

Indices 2, 6 and 9 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623 and 2, 5, 8 of df528a8a25a04cbd9fb1cc12319f3467 report other_leader_before_result false: no competing leader existed at the instant of the false confirmation, so the immediate harm shown here is a broken confirmation guarantee, not yet an observed stale read served under a competing leader.

The second vote that completes the quorum is attributed to the reachable non-voter by construction (the two controls change only suffrage and reachability); the internal verifyFuture.votes counter was not instrumented.

Only DemoteVoter was exercised as the voter-to-non-voter transition; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage follow the same Suffrage != Voter path in startStopReplication and notifyAll but were not executed.

Two of the three successor treatment attempts saw no far-side leader within the harness's 4s post-confirmation window, so the timing of the majority-side election relative to the leader's lease is only partially characterized.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons and their meaning, kept separate from the defect judgment. Comparison 0 (anomaly prediction: success with only the demoted non-voter reachable) holds on index 2. Comparison 1 (anomaly prediction for the extension, antecedent new_leader_exists true) holds on index 3: the same confirmation is answered with nil at 5509ms while a competing node holds leadership and while the answering leader is still Leader with a 20s lease. Comparison 2 (antecedent new_leader_fsm_has_write true, applicability old_leader_is_leader true) holds on index 4: the payload committed by the competing leader at index 5 is absent from the old leader's FSM, whose applied index is 3 — so a client that follows the documented pattern (confirm, then read) reads state that omits a committed write. Comparison 3 (control) holds on index 7: the identical construction and per-node timing without the demotion yields no competitor and no success, ending in leadership loss at 20003ms. Defect claim: the confirmation is computed against a voter-only quorum (raft.go:1086-1093) but credited by an unfiltered vote path (raft.go:965-987 registering every followerReplication; replication.go:100-111 notifying each; future.go:274-293 counting without suffrage), while the target's own definition states non-voters are not considered for elections or commitment (configuration.go:16-18); therefore a client can be told it is safe to treat a leader that has lost every other voter as leader for the whole configured lease interval, even after a different node holds leadership and has committed writes the old leader never received. The controls in the two earlier receipts (indices 12 and 15 of 68e243c33c644a32bc7ec9b29f076623, indices 11 and 14 of df528a8a25a04cbd9fb1cc12319f3467) already excluded reachability and kept the same reachable node as a voter, so the enabling property remains the unfiltered vote attribution.

answers.101498ecfbb945e0b48676dd9e9f4172-gap-0: Yes, and the bound is the leader's own lease rather than the election interval. In the extended-window execution the partitioned leader answered VerifyLeader successfully at 0ms and again at 5509ms (index 2 and 3), while the voter majority had already elected its own leader and committed a write at index 5 (index 4); the old leader remained Leader at applied index 3 with that write absent from its FSM. The lease path that eventually ends this state is checkLeaderLease, which counts only voters whose last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout (raft.go:1036-1060), so the window lasts as long as the configured lease; ValidateConfig only requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout (config.go:366-371), so the 20s used here is a legal configuration and the exposure is bounded by that configured value, not by the followers' 3s election time.

limitations: One treatment execution of the extended window (plus its control); the pre-window treatment was executed three times per receipt in the two earlier receipts, but the superseded-leader coincidence was observed once.

interpretations.rationale: Declared comparisons: six per-run predicates - every node converges within ten seconds, and no node's view is old while its own log already contains the configuration entry. All six are complete and hold, over twelve node observations in the successor receipt and the same measurements in the earlier one. Mechanism check against the source: a peer's own view is the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration, from processConfigurationLogEntry during appendEntries for newly appended entries, or from installSnapshot; the observed last_index_end of 3 on every node with config_index 3 shows every log did receive the entry, and the view followed within about one sample interval, so the entry-processing path is not the limiting factor and delivery was immediate. The suspicion that a demoted peer can hold the old suffrage for seconds on a healthy cluster is therefore defeated for this construction. What remains is a single unexplained observation from a different receipt (extended-window run, near_node_self_voter true after a bounded three second settle loop), which I keep recorded as a boundary rather than converting into a claim: it was not reproduced in four runs of the discriminating experiment, and the two structural differences I could identify between the harnesses were themselves exercised natively without reproducing it.

interpretations.rationale: What the observations establish: with a non-voter destination the transfer future returns nil (index 1, same millisecond, comparison 0 holds) although the destination never leads during the following eight seconds (index 2, comparison 1 holds) and the requested destination was the only node the caller named; simultaneously the old leader is already Follower and the target is Candidate, with the terms having advanced. The control shows the same call shape aimed at a voter returning nil and that voter actually leading (indices 4 and 5, comparisons 3 and 4 hold), so the difference is the destination's suffrage and not the API shape. The source path accounts for each part: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not filter the destination (raft.go:2184-2207) while pickServer does (raft.go:2163-2182); TimeoutNow turns the destination into a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote regardless of suffrage (raft.go:2209-2214); a voter receiving that candidate's RequestVote adopts the higher term and steps down before the suffrage check rejects the vote (raft.go:1660-1690), which is why the sitting leader loses leadership; and the transfer branch reports success on the leftLeaderLoop path without checking whether the requested destination became leader (raft.go:733-737). The claim is therefore scoped and conditional: a caller that names a destination which the configuration does not allow to lead receives a success result it cannot distinguish from a real handover, and in exchange the cluster suffers a leadership interruption and a fresh election that the caller did not request. The consequence is bounded - the cluster recovered in the same window, in this run by re-electing the very node it had just lost - and that recovery is the counterevidence that limits the phrasing rather than the mechanism.
counterevidence: Comparison 2 is violated by a valid witness: the emitted field old_leader_still_leader records that the old leader was observed leading during the eight second watch, because after the disruption it won the fresh election (index 2, leader_after_id is the old leader's own id). Any phrasing that leadership is lost for good, or that the cluster is left without a leader, is contradicted by this observation.

The watch samples states every 100ms, so a leaderless interval shorter than that interval inside the window would not be recorded; the receipt shows the interruption through index 1 (old leader Follower, target Candidate, nil result) rather than through a measured leaderless duration.

The nil result has two possible provenance paths in the transfer branch (the leader left the leaderLoop, or the wait for the destination timed out); this receipt shows the immediate return with the old leader already Follower and the target still Candidate, which matches the leftLeaderLoop path, but the harness does not read that branch directly.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control in the same run, uniform timings (HeartbeatTimeout 2s, LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s), in-memory transports in one process, fully connected throughout.
The destination is a node demoted through DemoteVoter; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage reach the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not exercised.
The caller's observation is the future's error value only; the harness does not attempt to distinguish a handover from a fresh election through any other client-visible signal.
The eight second watch bounds nothing about how long a leaderless interval could last in a cluster with slower timings or fewer reachable voters.

interpretations.rationale: What the corrected comparisons establish: (1) the transfer future reports success although the named destination holds no vote; (2) at the moment that success arrives the sitting leader is no longer Leader; (3) the named destination never leads during the watch; (4) the cluster is observed without a leader during the watch, so the existing leadership was interrupted rather than handed over; (5) the control with a voter destination reports success and that destination leads. Source-wise each step has an owner: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not filter the destination (raft.go:2184-2207) while pickServer does (raft.go:2163-2182); TimeoutNow turns the destination into a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote regardless of suffrage (raft.go:2209-2214); voters that receive its RequestVote adopt the higher term and step down before the suffrage check rejects the vote (raft.go:1660-1690), which is what removes the sitting leader; and the transfer branch reports success on the lost-leadership path without checking whether the requested destination became leader (raft.go:733-737). The defect claim is therefore: naming a destination the configuration does not allow to lead yields a success result indistinguishable from a real handover, while the sitting leadership is interrupted and a fresh election - which the caller did not ask for and which need not restore the same node - decides the outcome. The recovery is real and bounds the consequence (the cluster elected a new leader within the same eight second window), so nothing is claimed about sustained unavailability.
counterevidence: The interruption is bounded: in both receipts the cluster elected a leader again inside the watch window, and no leaderless interval longer than the watch is claimed, so any phrasing that the cluster is left unavailable is contradicted.

The earlier receipt's watch sampled every 100ms and recorded the old leader leading again inside the window; that observation remains true of that run but is not part of this account's predicates, which assert the destination and interruption instead.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control per receipt; uniform timings and fully connected in-memory transports in one process.

The success is attributed to the lost-leadership branch from the observable pattern (leader already Follower, destination still Candidate, result in about a millisecond) rather than by reading that branch.
Destination suffrage other than DemoteVoter (AddNonvoter, deprecated Staging) was not exercised.
The leaderless interval is detected by sampling, so its duration is not measured; only its occurrence is established.
interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts run the same fixed experiment family from identical inputs - cluster, timings, DemoteVoter step, transfer call, 15s future wait and 8s watch. The successor samples the watch every 20ms instead of 100ms and adds leaderless_seen so the interruption can be asserted directly; event indices 0, 1 and 4 carry the same measurements in both, index 2 is the same summary with the extra field, and the earlier receipt's violated predicate is not used by the corrected account.
